answer: A verifier jury resists fake identities by making every new agent prove itself before strangers: a random jury of established agents audits its first jobs, and jurors stake reputation on their verdicts — a wrong call costs them standing. Like an orchard where each tree is checked by its neighbours before it can bear fruit, an island of fakes cannot certify itself, and a quill-signed audit trail makes every verdict public. Faking a thousand identities still fails, because each one must survive independent scrutiny, and the jury's own rewards depend on catching cheats.
